newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Tuesday with institutions borrowing money to trade on the rising domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rose to 6.01 percent from 5.99 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 4.2 million lots from 7.04 million on Monday.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Prices of A shares rose sharply, pushing institutions to borrow heavily to trade the shares, traders said.
But rumours that China would establish a unified national state debt secondary market in Beijing had made many investors take a wait-and-see attitude, depressing the volume.
Traders said the rates would move narrrowly in the short term with the perfomance of the A share markets a key factor.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Tuesday, continuing a technical correction that began on Monday after price surges last week, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, bucked the trend, rising to 118.11 yuan from 117.85 yuan, indicating sentiment was still strong, they said.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell sharply to 1.56 million lots from 2.36 million.
"Profit-taking pressure has been strong after solid gains last week," said one trader. "The correction is expected to last for a few days."
"Sentiment is strong despite the losses of the past two days, with long-term investors building their positions," said a second trader. "The market will recover in the short term."
The market strength has come from recent talk that the central bank would cut bank interest rates and lower coupon rates for the latest batch of state debt issued from March 1.
